claims.text: Dijkstra published 'A note on two problems in connexion with graphs' in Numerische Mathematik volume 1, pages 269 to 271, in 1959.

source.title: Dijkstra, E. W., A note on two problems in connexion with graphs, Numerische Mathematik 1:269-271, 1959, DOI 10.1007/BF01386390

claims.text: The paper presents two problems. Problem 1 is the minimum spanning tree; Problem 2 is the shortest path between two nodes. The shortest path algorithm is the second of the two.

source.title: Dijkstra 1959, original text, CWI institutional repository scan

claims.text: Dijkstra's affiliation on the paper is Mathematisch Centrum, Amsterdam.

Dijkstra later recalled devising the algorithm in about twenty minutes in 1956, at a cafe terrace in Amsterdam, as a demonstration problem for the ARMAC computer, and publishing it three years afterwards. This is his own recollection given decades later, not a contemporaneous record.

source.title: Dijkstra's own later recollection of the ARMAC demonstration; self-reported, recorded long after the event

claims.text: The Bellman-Ford algorithm relaxes every edge repeatedly rather than settling nodes, and unlike Dijkstra it tolerates negative edge weights. The name comes from Richard Bellman's 'On A Routing Problem', Quarterly of Applied Mathematics 16.1 (1958), pages 87 to 90, and L. R. Ford Jr's RAND technical report P-923, 'Network Flow Theory', 1956.

source.title: Bellman, R., On A Routing Problem, Quarterly of Applied Mathematics 16.1:87-90, 1958; Ford, L. R. Jr., Network Flow Theory, RAND Technical Report P-923, 1956

claims.text: If a negative cycle is reachable from the source, the distance to some vertices is effectively negative infinity, and finding shortest simple paths in that setting is NP-hard. Implementations therefore report that a negative cycle exists rather than attempting to route around it.

source.title: Cherkassky, B. V. and Goldberg, A. V., Negative-cycle detection algorithms, Mathematical Programming 85(2):277-311, 1999

beats.broke: no systematic way to find a cheapest route; search the paths and the count explodes
beats.fix: Dijkstra 1956, published 1959: settle the nearest unsettled node, repeatedly
beats.cost: requires non-negative weights; a priority queue; explores outward in all directions
beats.interview: why negative edges break it, and what you use instead
